definitions.explanation: Traditional practices or behaviors passed down in a community or society.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{風習|ふうしゅう}が{残|のこ}っている。
{地域|ちいき}の{風習|ふうしゅう}に{従|したが}う。
{日本|にほん}の{風習|ふうしゅう}を{学|まな}ぶ。

notes:
{風習|ふうしゅう} refers to customs and traditional practices that have been passed down within a community or region over time. It emphasizes the social and cultural nature of the practice rather than individual habit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風習|ふうしゅう}に{従|したが}う: to follow customs
- {古|ふる}い{風習|ふうしゅう}: old customs
- {地域|ちいき}の{風習|ふうしゅう}: local customs
- {風習|ふうしゅう}が{残|のこ}る: customs remain/survive
- {風習|ふうしゅう}が{廃|すた}れる: customs die out

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {習慣|しゅうかん}: habit or custom (can be personal or social)
- {慣習|かんしゅう}: convention, established practice (more formal/institutional)
- {伝統|でんとう}: tradition (broader, emphasizes continuity and value)
- {風俗|ふうぞく}: manners and customs (often refers to the general customs of a time or place; also has a modern meaning of adult entertainment industry)

{風習|ふうしゅう} is most natural when talking about specific regional or cultural practices, such as seasonal festivals, wedding ceremonies, or local rituals.
